day_set_equivalence.rule_in_compute_daily_rank_ic: rank_ic_valid is set only when len(scored) >= minimum_cross_section AND (not enforce_score_health OR score_health_valid); with include_invalid=False the invalid rows are dropped before summarize_rank_ic, with include_invalid=True they are kept but summarize_rank_ic filters on rank_ic_valid & finite -- so both average over exactly the same set of days

the_duplicate_definition.verdict: the two agree today, so the numbers are consistent -- but the shared module's docstring says it exists so the metric is 'defined once', and the largest consumer does not use it, so that guarantee currently holds by coincidence rather than by construction

criteria_enumerated: coverage and score_std must both be finite reals (a non-finite value fails the day)
unique_score_count must be an Integral and not a bool (a type guard, not a threshold)

0.90 <= coverage <= 1.0  -- the floor §K and §AG already identified; the upper bound is defensive, since coverage = len(scored)/valid_label_count over a left merge from the labels and therefore cannot exceed 1.0
unique_score_count >= 10  -- a day on which the model emits fewer than ten distinct scores is rejected even if it covers the cross-section
score_std > 1e-6  -- a day on which the scores are numerically constant is rejected
what_require_score_health_true_adds.open_item_wording: 没有核对 require_score_health=True 在 OOS 路径上除覆盖率之外还启用了哪些判据
what_require_score_health_true_adds.reading: the OOS acceptance path therefore filters days on three numeric criteria, not one. Any day the candidate scores thinly (fewer than ten distinct values) or flatly (std at or below 1e-6) is excluded from the OOS mean_rank_ic while the same day would still count in a validation mean_rank_ic. That is a second, independent reason the two sides are not the same estimator, on top of the coverage floor.

who_selects_the_winner.dead_code_test: a function is production-dead here if no non-test file imports it and no non-test file names it outside its own definition; tests are excluded from the scan by path, so a test-only function still counts as dead
